answer: A practical defense is mutual attestation bonds: every new identity must lock a small stake and collect endorsements from several established peers before it can transact. Endorsers vouch their own stake, so they inspect newcomers carefully. Like a lantern lit in a dark meadow, each bond makes the identity visible; an attacker running an orchard of fake selves must pay a fresh bond and pass inspection for every one, and abandoned bonds decay to zero. Fakes become expensive to mint and costly to maintain, so honest agents outnumber them.
